body.en: Euclidean Invariants, Locus Equations & Scaling Laws: In analytic geometry, geometric loci translate into algebraic constraints via Euclidean distance \(d = \sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2 + (y_2-y_1)^2}\). A circle of center \((h, k)\) and radius \(r\) satisfies \((x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2\), and a tangent line at point \(P\) is strictly perpendicular to the radius \(CP\) (\(m_{\text{tan}} \cdot m_{\text{rad}} = -1\)). Under a similarity scale factor \(k\), all linear lengths scale by \(k\), surface areas scale by \(k^2\), and volumes scale by \(k^3\).
body.ar: Euclidean Invariants, Locus المعادلات & Scaling Laws: In analytic الهندسة, geometric loci translate into algebraic constraints via Euclidean distance \(d = \sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2 + (y_2-y_1)^2}\). A الدائرة of center \((h, k)\) and نصف القطر \(r\) satisfies \((x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2\), and a خط المماس at point \(P\) is strictly perpendicular to the نصف القطر \(CP\) (\(m_{\text{tan}} \cdot m_{\text{rad}} = -1\)). Under a similarity scale factor \(k\), all linear lengths scale by \(k\), surface areas scale by \(k^2\), and volumes scale by \(k^3\).

body.en:
Why Inscribed Angles Equal Half the Central Angle & Circle Completion Works: Given \(x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\), completing the square in \(x\) and \(y\) simultaneously yields:

\[ (x + g)^2 - g^2 + (y + f)^2 - f^2 + c = 0 \implies (x + g)^2 + (y + f)^2 = g^2 + f^2 - c \]

Thus the center is \((-g, -f)\) and the radius is \(r = \sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c}\) (requiring \(g^2 + f^2 > c\)). In any circle, drawing diameter \(POQ\) splits an inscribed angle \(\angle APB\) into two isosceles triangles \(\triangle OAP\) and \(\triangle OBP\) (since \(OA = OB = OP = r\)); by the exterior angle theorem, \(\angle AOB = 2\angle APB\).
body.ar:
Why Inscribed Angles Equal Half the Central الزاوية & الدائرة Completion Works: المعطيات \(x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\), completing the square in \(x\) and \(y\) simultaneously yields:

\[ (x + g)^2 - g^2 + (y + f)^2 - f^2 + c = 0 \implies (x + g)^2 + (y + f)^2 = g^2 + f^2 - c \]

Thus the center is \((-g, -f)\) and the نصف القطر is \(r = \sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c}\) (requiring \(g^2 + f^2 > c\)). In any الدائرة, drawing القطر \(POQ\) splits an inscribed الزاوية \(\angle APB\) into two isosceles triangles \(\triangle OAP\) and \(\triangle OBP\) (since \(OA = OB = OP = r\)); by the exterior الزاوية المبرهنة, \(\angle AOB = 2\angle APB\).

body.en:
Line \( L_1 \) passes through \( (1, 2) \) and \( (4, 8) \). Find the slope of a line \( L_2 \) perpendicular to \( L_1 \).

First compute the slope of \( L_1 \):

\[ m_1 = \frac{8 - 2}{4 - 1} = \frac{6}{3} = 2. \]

Perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals: \( m_1 \cdot m_2 = -1 \):

\[ m_2 = -\frac{1}{m_1} = -\frac{1}{2}. \]
body.ar:
Line \( L_1 \) passes through \( (1, 2) \) and \( (4, 8) \). أوجد ميل a line \( L_2 \) perpendicular to \( L_1 \).

First compute the الميل of \( L_1 \):

\[ m_1 = \frac{8 - 2}{4 - 1} = \frac{6}{3} = 2. \]

Perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals: \( m_1 \cdot m_2 = -1 \):

\[ m_2 = -\frac{1}{m_1} = -\frac{1}{2}. \]

body.en: A common mistake is taking only the negative of the slope without inverting it (e.g. thinking the perpendicular slope to \( 3 \) is \( -3 \)). Perpendicular lines have negative reciprocals: both flip the sign and invert the fraction (\( 3 \to -\tfrac{1}{3} \)). Special case: horizontal lines (\( m = 0 \)) are perpendicular to vertical lines (slope undefined).
body.ar: A common mistake is taking only the negative of the الميل without inverting it (e.g. thinking the perpendicular الميل to \( 3 \) is \( -3 \)). Perpendicular lines have negative reciprocals: both flip the sign and invert the fraction (\( 3 \to -\tfrac{1}{3} \)). Special case: horizontal lines (\( m = 0 \)) are perpendicular to vertical lines (الميل undefined).

body.en:
Problem (Hard): In the \(xy\)-plane, a parabola \(\mathcal{P}\) is defined as the set of all points equidistant from the focus \(F(1, 2)\) and the directrix line \(y = -2\). The line \(x - y = 1\) intersects \(\mathcal{P}\) at two distinct points, \(A\) and \(B\). What is the length of the segment \(AB\)?

Step-by-Step Solution: Step 1: Derive the equation of the parabola \(\mathcal{P}\) using the focus-directrix definition. By definition, any point \(P(x, y)\) on the parabola satisfies: \[ \text{distance}(P, F) = \text{distance}(P, \text{directrix}) \] The distance from \((x, y)\) to \(F(1, 2)\) is \(\sqrt{(x - 1)^2 + (y - 2)^2}\), and the perpendicular distance to the directrix \(y = -2\) is \(|y - (-2)| = |y + 2|\). Equating the squared distances: \[ (x - 1)^2 + (y - 2)^2 = (y + 2)^2 \] Expanding the terms involving \(y\): \[ (x - 1)^2 + y^2 - 4y + 4 = y^2 + 4y + 4 \] Subtracting \(y^2 + 4\) from both sides and simplifying: \[ (x - 1)^2 = 8y \implies y = \frac{(x - 1)^2}{8} \] Step 2: Find the intersection points of the parabola and the line \(x - y = 1\). From the line's equation, \(y = x - 1\). Substitute this into the parabola's equation: \[ x - 1 = \frac{(x - 1)^2}{8} \] \[ 8(x - 1) = (x - 1)^2 \] \[ (x - 1)^2 - 8(x - 1) = 0 \implies (x - 1)(x - 1 - 8) = 0 \] Thus, \(x - 1 = 0\) or \(x - 9 = 0\), yielding \(x = 1\) or \(x = 9\). Step 3: Determine the coordinates of \(A\) and \(B\). - For \(x = 1\): \(y = 1 - 1 = 0\), so \(A = (1, 0)\). - For \(x = 9\): \(y = 9 - 1 = 8\), so \(B = (9, 8)\). Step 4: Compute the length of segment \(AB\). \[ AB = \sqrt{(9 - 1)^2 + (8 - 0)^2} = \sqrt{8^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{64 + 64} = \sqrt{128} = 8\sqrt{2} \] Misconception Analysis: - Choice A (\(4\sqrt{2}\)) results from incorrectly using \(4p = 4\) instead of \(4p = 8\) (where \(p = 2\) is the directed distance from vertex to focus). - Choice B (\(8\)) results from computing only the horizontal change \(\Delta x = 9 - 1 = 8\) instead of the Euclidean distance. - Choice D (\(16\)) results from computing the taxicab/Manhattan distance \(|\Delta x| + |\Delta y| = 8 + 8 = 16\).
body.ar:
Problem (Hard): In the \(xy\)-plane, a القطع المكافئ \(\mathcal{P}\) is defined as the set of all points equidistant from the focus \(F(1, 2)\) and the directrix line \(y = -2\). The line \(x - y = 1\) intersects \(\mathcal{P}\) at two distinct points, \(A\) and \(B\). What is the length of the segment \(AB\)?

Step-by-Step الحل: الخطوة ١: Derive the المعادلة of the القطع المكافئ \(\mathcal{P}\) using the focus-directrix definition. By definition, any point \(P(x, y)\) on the القطع المكافئ satisfies: \[ \text{distance}(P, F) = \text{distance}(P, \text{directrix}) \] The distance from \((x, y)\) to \(F(1, 2)\) is \(\sqrt{(x - 1)^2 + (y - 2)^2}\), and the perpendicular distance to the directrix \(y = -2\) is \(|y - (-2)| = |y + 2|\). Equating the squared distances: \[ (x - 1)^2 + (y - 2)^2 = (y + 2)^2 \] Expanding the terms involving \(y\): \[ (x - 1)^2 + y^2 - 4y + 4 = y^2 + 4y + 4 \] Subtracting \(y^2 + 4\) from both sides and simplifying: \[ (x - 1)^2 = 8y \implies y = \frac{(x - 1)^2}{8} \] الخطوة ٢: أوجد التقاطع points of the القطع المكافئ and the line \(x - y = 1\). From the line's المعادلة, \(y = x - 1\). عوّض this into the القطع المكافئ's المعادلة: \[ x - 1 = \frac{(x - 1)^2}{8} \] \[ 8(x - 1) = (x - 1)^2 \] \[ (x - 1)^2 - 8(x - 1) = 0 \implies (x - 1)(x - 1 - 8) = 0 \] وعليه, \(x - 1 = 0\) or \(x - 9 = 0\), yielding \(x = 1\) or \(x = 9\). الخطوة ٣: حدّد الإحداثيات of \(A\) and \(B\). - For \(x = 1\): \(y = 1 - 1 = 0\), so \(A = (1, 0)\). - For \(x = 9\): \(y = 9 - 1 = 8\), so \(B = (9, 8)\). الخطوة ٤: Compute the length of segment \(AB\). \[ AB = \sqrt{(9 - 1)^2 + (8 - 0)^2} = \sqrt{8^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{64 + 64} = \sqrt{128} = 8\sqrt{2} \] Misconception Analysis: - Choice A (\(4\sqrt{2}\)) results from incorrectly using \(4p = 4\) instead of \(4p = 8\) (حيث \(p = 2\) is the directed distance from الرأس to focus). - Choice B (\(8\)) results from computing only the horizontal change \(\Delta x = 9 - 1 = 8\) instead of the Euclidean distance. - Choice D (\(16\)) results from computing the taxicab/Manhattan distance \(|\Delta x| + |\Delta y| = 8 + 8 = 16\).

body.en:
Problem (Easy): Which of the following is an equation of the line that passes through the point \((4, -1)\) and is perpendicular to the line \(y = 2x + 3\)?

Step-by-Step Solution: To find the equation of the line perpendicular to \(y = 2x + 3\), first determine the required slope. The given line has a slope of \(m_1 = 2\). Two non-vertical lines are perpendicular if and only if the product of their slopes is \(-1\) (i.e., their slopes are negative reciprocals): \[m_2 = -\frac{1}{m_1} = -\frac{1}{2}\] Next, use the point-slope form \(y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)\) with the point \((x_1, y_1) = (4, -1)\) and slope \(m = -\frac{1}{2}\): \[y - (-1) = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 4)\] \[y + 1 = -\frac{1}{2}x + 2\] \[y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 1\] Common misconceptions: - Choosing \(y = 2x - 9\) incorrectly uses the parallel slope (\(m = 2\)) instead of the perpendicular slope. - Choosing \(y = \frac{1}{2}x - 3\) takes the reciprocal of the slope but forgets to negate it. - Choosing \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x - 3\) makes an algebraic sign error when solving \(-1 = -\frac{1}{2}(4) + b\).
body.ar:
Problem (Easy): Which of the following is an المعادلة of the line that passes through the point \((4, -1)\) and is perpendicular to the line \(y = 2x + 3\)?

Step-by-Step الحل: To أوجد معادلة the line perpendicular to \(y = 2x + 3\), first حدّد required الميل. The المعطيات line has a الميل of \(m_1 = 2\). Two non-vertical lines are perpendicular if and only if the product of their slopes is \(-1\) (i.e., their slopes are negative reciprocals): \[m_2 = -\frac{1}{m_1} = -\frac{1}{2}\] Next, use the point-الميل form \(y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)\) with the point \((x_1, y_1) = (4, -1)\) and الميل \(m = -\frac{1}{2}\): \[y - (-1) = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 4)\] \[y + 1 = -\frac{1}{2}x + 2\] \[y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 1\] Common misconceptions: - Choosing \(y = 2x - 9\) incorrectly uses the parallel الميل (\(m = 2\)) instead of the perpendicular الميل. - Choosing \(y = \frac{1}{2}x - 3\) takes the reciprocal of the الميل but forgets to negate it. - Choosing \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x - 3\) makes an algebraic sign error عندما solving \(-1 = -\frac{1}{2}(4) + b\).

question.en: Segment \( AB \) has endpoints \( A(2, -1) \) and \( B(6, 7) \). Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of \( AB \) in slope-intercept form.
question.ar: Segment \( AB \) has endpoints \( A(2, -1) \) and \( B(6, 7) \). أوجد equation of the perpendicular bisector of \( AB \) in slope-intercept form.

solution.en:
Solution: The perpendicular bisector passes through the midpoint and has a perpendicular slope.

Step 1 (Midpoint):

\[ M = \left(\frac{2 + 6}{2},\ \frac{-1 + 7}{2}\right) = (4, 3). \]

Step 2 (Slope of AB):

\[ m_{AB} = \frac{7 - (-1)}{6 - 2} = \frac{8}{4} = 2. \]

Step 3 (Perpendicular slope):

\[ m_{\perp} = -\frac{1}{2}. \]

Step 4 (Point-slope equation through M(4, 3)):

\[ y - 3 = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 4) \implies y - 3 = -\frac{1}{2}x + 2 \implies y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 5. \]
solution.ar:
Solution: The perpendicular bisector يمر بالنقطة the midpoint and has a perpendicular slope.

Step 1 (Midpoint):

\[ M = \left(\frac{2 + 6}{2},\ \frac{-1 + 7}{2}\right) = (4, 3). \]

Step 2 (Slope of AB):

\[ m_{AB} = \frac{7 - (-1)}{6 - 2} = \frac{8}{4} = 2. \]

Step 3 (Perpendicular slope):

\[ m_{\perp} = -\frac{1}{2}. \]

Step 4 (Point-slope equation through M(4, 3)):

\[ y - 3 = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 4) \implies y - 3 = -\frac{1}{2}x + 2 \implies y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 5. \]

question.en: Find the coordinates of the point \(P\) on directed line segment from \(A(-3, 2)\) to \(B(7, 12)\) that partitions the segment in the ratio \(2 : 3\).
question.ar: أوجد إحداثيات the point \(P\) on directed line segment from \(A(-3, 2)\) to \(B(7, 12)\) that partitions the segment in the ratio \(2 : 3\).

solution.en:
Step 1: Determine the fractional distance: A ratio of \(2 : 3\) means \(P\) is \(\frac{2}{2 + 3} = \frac{2}{5}\) of the way from \(A\) to \(B\).

Step 2: Apply the partition formula:

\[ x_P = x_1 + \frac{2}{5}(x_2 - x_1) = -3 + \frac{2}{5}(7 - (-3)) = -3 + \frac{2}{5}(10) = -3 + 4 = 1. \]\[ y_P = y_1 + \frac{2}{5}(y_2 - y_1) = 2 + \frac{2}{5}(12 - 2) = 2 + \frac{2}{5}(10) = 2 + 4 = 6. \]

The partitioning point is \(P(1, 6)\).

question.en: [Practice 3 · Medium] In the coordinate plane, quadrilateral \(ABCD\) has vertices \(A(-2, 3)\), \(B(4, 5)\), \(C(6, -1)\), and \(D(0, -3)\). Which of the following correctly classifies quadrilateral \(ABCD\) and gives its exact area?
question.ar: [Practice 3 · Medium] In the coordinate plane, quadrilateral \(ABCD\) has vertices \(A(-2, 3)\), \(B(4, 5)\), \(C(6, -1)\), and \(D(0, -3)\). Which of the following correctly classإذا كانies quadrilateral \(ABCD\) and gives its exact area?

hints.en: To classify quadrilateral \(ABCD\) and determine its area, we examine its side lengths, slopes, and dimensions: 1. Side Lengths (Distance Formula):
hints.ar: To classإذا كانy quadrilateral \(ABCD\) and حدّد its area, we examine its side lengths, slopes, and dimensions: 1. Side Lengths (Distance Formula):

hints.en: Thus, \(ABCD\) is a square with an area of \(40\).
hints.ar: وعليه، \(ABCD\) is a square with an area of \(40\).

solution.en:
To classify quadrilateral \(ABCD\) and determine its area, we examine its side lengths, slopes, and dimensions:

1. **Side Lengths (Distance Formula):**
- \(AB = \sqrt{(4 - (-2))^2 + (5 - 3)^2} = \sqrt{6^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{36 + 4} = \sqrt{40}\)
- \(BC = \sqrt{(6 - 4)^2 + (-1 - 5)^2} = \sqrt{2^2 + (-6)^2} = \sqrt{4 + 36} = \sqrt{40}\)
- \(CD = \sqrt{(0 - 6)^2 + (-3 - (-1))^2} = \sqrt{(-6)^2 + (-2)^2} = \sqrt{36 + 4} = \sqrt{40}\)
- \(DA = \sqrt{(-2 - 0)^2 + (3 - (-3))^2} = \sqrt{(-2)^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{4 + 36} = \sqrt{40}\)

Since all four sides are congruent (\(AB = BC = CD = DA = \sqrt{40}\)), \(ABCD\) is a rhombus.

2. **Slopes of Adjacent Sides:**
- Slope of \(AB = \frac{5 - 3}{4 - (-2)} = \frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}\)
- Slope of \(BC = \frac{-1 - 5}{6 - 4} = \frac{-6}{2} = -3\)

Since the product of their slopes is \(\frac{1}{3} \times (-3) = -1\), side \(AB\) is perpendicular to side \(BC\) (\(\angle B = 90^\circ\)). A rhombus with a right angle is a **square**.

3. **Area:**
- Direct formula: \(\text{Area} = (\text{side})^2 = (\sqrt{40})^2 = 40\).
- Box Method: The bounding rectangle enclosing \(ABCD\) spans from \(x = -2\) to \(x = 6\) (width \(8\)) and \(y = -3\) to \(y = 5\) (height \(8\)), with total area \(8 \times 8 = 64\). Subtracting the four corner right triangles, each with legs \(6\) and \(2\) and area \(\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 2 = 6\):
\[\text{Area} = 64 - 4(6) = 64 - 24 = 40.\]

Thus, \(ABCD\) is a square with an area of \(40\).

**Common Misconceptions:**
- Choice B is incorrect because it fails to recognize that all four sides are equal, which makes the rectangle specifically a square.
- Choice C is incorrect because it overlooks that the adjacent sides are perpendicular (product of slopes is \(-1\)).
- Choice D mistakenly takes the area of the bounding box (\(8 \times 8 = 64\)) without subtracting the surrounding corner triangles.
solution.ar:
To classإذا كانy quadrilateral \(ABCD\) and حدّد its area, we examine its side lengths, slopes, and dimensions:

1. **Side Lengths (Distance Formula):**
- \(AB = \sqrt{(4 - (-2))^2 + (5 - 3)^2} = \sqrt{6^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{36 + 4} = \sqrt{40}\)
- \(BC = \sqrt{(6 - 4)^2 + (-1 - 5)^2} = \sqrt{2^2 + (-6)^2} = \sqrt{4 + 36} = \sqrt{40}\)
- \(CD = \sqrt{(0 - 6)^2 + (-3 - (-1))^2} = \sqrt{(-6)^2 + (-2)^2} = \sqrt{36 + 4} = \sqrt{40}\)
- \(DA = \sqrt{(-2 - 0)^2 + (3 - (-3))^2} = \sqrt{(-2)^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{4 + 36} = \sqrt{40}\)

Since all four sides are congruent (\(AB = BC = CD = DA = \sqrt{40}\)), \(ABCD\) is a rhombus.

2. **Slopes of Adjacent Sides:**
- Slope of \(AB = \frac{5 - 3}{4 - (-2)} = \frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}\)
- Slope of \(BC = \frac{-1 - 5}{6 - 4} = \frac{-6}{2} = -3\)

Since the product of their slopes is \(\frac{1}{3} \times (-3) = -1\), side \(AB\) is عمودي على side \(BC\) (\(\angle B = 90^\circ\)). A rhombus with a right angle is a **square**.

3. **Area:**
- Direct formula: \(\text{Area} = (\text{side})^2 = (\sqrt{40})^2 = 40\).
- Box Method: The bounding rectangle enclosing \(ABCD\) spans from \(x = -2\) to \(x = 6\) (width \(8\)) and \(y = -3\) to \(y = 5\) (height \(8\)), with total area \(8 \times 8 = 64\). Subtracting the four corner right triangles, each with legs \(6\) and \(2\) and area \(\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 2 = 6\):
\[\text{Area} = 64 - 4(6) = 64 - 24 = 40.\]

وعليه، \(ABCD\) is a square with an area of \(40\).

**Common Misconceptions:**
- Choice B is incorrect because it fails to recognize that all four sides are equal, which makes the rectangle specإذا كانically a square.
- Choice C is incorrect because it overlooks that the adjacent sides are perpendicular (product of slopes is \(-1\)).
- Choice D mistakenly takes the area of the bounding box (\(8 \times 8 = 64\)) without subtracting the surrounding corner triangles.

question.en: [Practice 4 · Hard] Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, forming a pair of corresponding angles \((4x+16)^\circ\) and \((2x+26)^\circ\). Find the measure of each angle.
question.ar: [Practice 4 · Hard] Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, forming a pair of corresponding angles \((4x+16)^\circ\) and \((2x+26)^\circ\). أوجد measure of each angle.

hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(4x+16=2x+26\) لتبسيط الخطوة.
تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(x=5\) لتبسيط الخطوة.
تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(= 4(5)+16\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

solution.en: Corresponding angles are equal: \(4x+16=2x+26\). Solving gives \(x=5\), so each angle \(=4(5)+16=36^\circ\).

question.en: [Practice 5 · Easy] Consider the line \(L\) with the equation \(3x - 4y + 15 = 0\). A point \(P\) has coordinates \((5, -2)\). Calculate the shortest perpendicular distance from point \(P\) to line \(L\).
question.ar: [Practice 5 · Easy] Consider the line \(L\) with the equation \(3x - 4y + 15 = 0\). A point \(P\) has coordinates \((5, -2)\). احسب shortest perpendicular distance from point \(P\) to line \(L\).

hints.en: The formula for the shortest perpendicular distance from a point \((x_0, y_0)\) to a line \(Ax + By + C = 0\) is given by \(d = \frac{|Ax_0 + By_0 + C|}{\sqrt{A^2 + B^2}}\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \((x_0, y_0)\) ، \(Ax + By + C = 0\) ، \(d = \frac{|Ax_0 + By_0 + C|}{\sqrt{A^2 + B^2}}\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: In this problem, the point \(P\) has coordinates \((x_0, y_0) = (5, -2)\) and the line \(L\) is \(3x - 4y + 15 = 0\). Thus, \(A = 3\), \(B = -4\), and \(C = 15\). Substituting these values into the distance formula: \(d = \frac{|(3)(5) + (-4)(-2) + 15|}{\sqrt{3^2 + (-4)^2}}\).
hints.ar: In this problem, the point \(P\) has coordinates \((x_0, y_0) = (5, -2)\) and the line \(L\) is \(3x - 4y + 15 = 0\). وعليه، \(A = 3\), \(B = -4\), and \(C = 15\). Substituting these values into the distance formula: \(d = \frac{|(3)(5) + (-4)(-2) + 15|}{\sqrt{3^2 + (-4)^2}}\).

hints.en: Therefore, the shortest perpendicular distance from point \(P\) to line \(L\) is \(\frac{38}{5}\).
hints.ar: وبالتالي، the shortest perpendicular distance from point \(P\) to line \(L\) is \(\frac{38}{5}\).

solution.en:
The formula for the shortest perpendicular distance from a point \((x_0, y_0)\) to a line \(Ax + By + C = 0\) is given by \(d = \frac{|Ax_0 + By_0 + C|}{\sqrt{A^2 + B^2}}\).
In this problem, the point \(P\) has coordinates \((x_0, y_0) = (5, -2)\) and the line \(L\) is \(3x - 4y + 15 = 0\). Thus, \(A = 3\), \(B = -4\), and \(C = 15\).
Substituting these values into the distance formula:
\(d = \frac{|(3)(5) + (-4)(-2) + 15|}{\sqrt{3^2 + (-4)^2}}\)
\(d = \frac{|15 + 8 + 15|}{\sqrt{9 + 16}}\)
\(d = \frac{|38|}{\sqrt{25}}\)
\(d = \frac{38}{5}\)
Therefore, the shortest perpendicular distance from point \(P\) to line \(L\) is \(\frac{38}{5}\).

label.en: ● Master Atlas of the 9 Main Parent Functions & Universal Transformation Law
label.ar: ● الأطلس الشامل للدوال الأم التسع وقانون التحويلات الهندسية العام

body.en:
Every algebraic and elementary transcendental model is built by transforming one of the nine core parent functions via \(g(x) = a\,f(x - h) + k\), where \(|a|\) scales vertically (reflecting across the \(x\)-axis if \(a < 0\)), \(h\) shifts horizontally, and \(k\) shifts vertically:

FamilyTransformed Form \(g(x)\)DomainRange (\(a > 0\))Key Geometric Feature
Constant\(f(x) = c\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\{c\}\)Horizontal line, slope \(0\)
Linear\(a(x - h) + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Constant slope \(m = a\), pivot \((h, k)\)
Quadratic\(a(x - h)^2 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)Parabola vertex \((h, k)\), axis \(x = h\)
Cubic\(a(x - h)^3 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Inflection center \((h, k)\), S-curve
Absolute Value\(a|x - h| + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)V-corner vertex \((h, k)\), slopes \(\pm a\)
Radical\(a\sqrt{x - h} + k\)\([h, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)Endpoint \((h, k)\), half-parabola
Rational\(\dfrac{a}{x - h} + k\)\(x \neq h\)\(y \neq k\)Vertical asymptote \(x = h\), horizontal \(y = k\)
Exponential\(a \cdot 2^{x - h} + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((k, \infty)\)Horizontal asymptote \(y = k\), anchor \((h, a+k)\)
Logarithmic\(a\ln(x - h) + k\)\((h, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Vertical asymptote \(x = h\), anchor \((h+1, k)\)
body.ar:
تُبنى النماذج الجبرية والمتسامية الأساسية من خلال تطبيق التحويل القياسي \(g(x) = a\,f(x - h) + k\) على إحدى الدوال الأم التسع، حيث يتحكم \(|a|\) في التمدد الرأسي (مع انعكاس حول محور السينات إذا كان \(a < 0\))، ويمثل \(h\) الإزاحة الأفقية، و\(k\) الإزاحة الرأسية:

عائلة الدالةالصورة المحوّلة \(g(x)\)المجالالمدى (\(a > 0\))السمة الهندسية المميزة
الثابتة\(f(x) = c\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\{c\}\)مستقيم أفقي ميله \(0\)
الخطية\(a(x - h) + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)ميل ثابت \(m = a\) ونقطة ارتكاز \((h, k)\)
التربيعية\(a(x - h)^2 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)قطع مكافئ رأسه \((h, k)\) ومحوره \(x = h\)
التكعيبية\(a(x - h)^3 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)نقطة انعطاف مركزية \((h, k)\)
القيمة المطلقة\(a|x - h| + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)رأس زاوي على شكل V عند \((h, k)\) بميلين \(\pm a\)
الجذرية\(a\sqrt{x - h} + k\)\([h, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)نقطة بداية \((h, k)\) ومجال مقيّد \(x \ge h\)
النسبية (المقلوب)\(\dfrac{a}{x - h} + k\)\(x \neq h\)\(y \neq k\)تقارب رأسي \(x = h\) وتقارب أفقي \(y = k\)
الأسية\(a \cdot 2^{x - h} + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((k, \infty)\)تقارب أفقي \(y = k\) ونقطة ارتكاز \((h, a+k)\)
اللوغاريتمية\(a\ln(x - h) + k\)\((h, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)تقارب رأسي \(x = h\) ونقطة ارتكاز \((h+1, k)\)
